question: Why do screenwriters often have the hero do a small kindness in the very first minutes?
answer: So the audience decides to be on their side. Blake Snyder named it the save-the-cat scene: an early act, like rescuing a pet or sharing food, that wins sympathy before the hero does anything difficult or dubious. Viewers then forgive later flaws, because a first impression of character sets how every later scene is read.
move: Early small acts set how everything later is judged.
ask: What small first impression am I giving people that will colour how they judge me later?
reference: Blake Snyder, Save the Cat! The Last Book on Screenwriting You'll Ever Need, Michael Wiese Productions, 2005
